summary: This is a test file that checks the RobotPet class behaves as expected. It uses Python's built-in unittest module to create a small set of automated checks that run every time you execute the file.

lines.text: A test class inherits from unittest.TestCase, which is what gives you the assert methods and lets the test runner discover the class.
setUp runs before every single test method, so each test gets its own freshly built pet and no test can be affected by changes another test made.
Every test method's name must begin with test_, or unittest will silently skip it — this is the most common reason a beginner's test "passes" without running.
assertIn checks that the name appears somewhere inside the returned text, which is more robust than demanding the whole sentence match exactly.
Asserting what should not be there catches a real bug: a talent hard-coded to one name would still pass the earlier tests but fail here.
This hands control to the test runner, which finds every test_ method in the file, runs them, and prints a dot per pass along with a summary.
